S — Situation

A 50-year-old patient is postoperative day 0 following an uncomplicated anterior cervical discectomy and fusion at C5–C6 for cervical disc prolapse with spinal cord and nerve-root compression. The patient is awake, haemodynamically stable, and neurologically intact compared with the preoperative baseline.

Current priorities are continued neurological observation, airway and swallowing assessment, pain management, wound monitoring, and early mobilisation as directed by the neurosurgical team.

Current vital signs: Blood pressure 132/78 mmHg, heart rate 82 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, temperature 36.7 °C.
Immediate concerns: Monitor for new limb weakness or sensory loss, airway compromise, neck swelling or haematoma, dysphagia, voice changes, uncontrolled pain, wound bleeding, and postoperative infection.

P — Patient Background

* Age: 50 years.
* Primary diagnosis: C5–C6 cervical disc prolapse causing cervical radiculopathy and early myelopathic symptoms.
* Procedure performed: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion with insertion of an interbody cage, anterior plate, and screws at C5–C6.
* Operated level: C5–C6.
* Indication: Persistent neck pain and right upper-limb radicular pain with progressive hand numbness and reduced grip strength despite conservative treatment.
* Presenting symptoms: Six-month history of neck pain radiating to the right shoulder and arm, paraesthesia affecting the thumb and index finger, and difficulty with fine hand movements. No preoperative bowel or bladder dysfunction.
* Relevant medical history: Hypertension controlled with amlodipine 5 mg once daily. No diabetes, cardiac disease, or previous spinal surgery. No known drug allergies. The patient was not taking anticoagulants or antiplatelet medication.
* Preoperative neurological status: Alert and oriented. Right hand grip 4+/5, right wrist extension 4+/5, and remaining upper- and lower-limb muscle groups 5/5. Mildly reduced sensation in the right C6 dermatome. Gait was independent. No bowel or bladder disturbance.
* Imaging: MRI demonstrated a C5–C6 posterolateral disc protrusion with foraminal narrowing and mild anterior indentation of the spinal cord, greater on the right side. No significant cord signal change was reported.
* Intraoperative course: Procedure completed under general anaesthesia without reported complications. Intraoperative neuromonitoring remained stable. Estimated blood loss was approximately 50 mL. No dural tear or cerebrospinal fluid leak was reported.
* Implant: Interbody cage packed with bone graft, anterior cervical plate, and four fixation screws at C5–C6. Implant position was satisfactory on intraoperative imaging.
* Drain: One small closed-suction drain placed in the anterior neck wound, with minimal serosanguineous output.
* Postoperative plan: Continue neurological and airway observations, maintain the wound dressing, monitor drain output, provide multimodal analgesia, mobilise with assistance when fully awake, and obtain postoperative cervical spine radiographs as requested by the surgeon.

A — Assessment

1. General condition

* General appearance and level of consciousness: Awake, alert, calm, and responding appropriately. No acute distress.
* GCS: 15/15.
* Blood pressure: 132/78 mmHg.
* Heart rate: 82 beats/min.
* Respiratory rate: 16 breaths/min.
* Oxygen saturation: 98% on room air.
* Temperature: 36.7 °C.
* Pain score: 4/10 at the anterior neck incision.
* Pain control: Adequate after prescribed intravenous analgesia. No severe radicular pain reported.

2. Neurological assessment

* Right upper-limb motor power: Shoulder abduction 5/5, elbow flexion 5/5, elbow extension 5/5, wrist extension 5/5, wrist flexion 5/5, finger abduction 5/5, and hand grip 5/5.
* Left upper-limb motor power: Shoulder abduction 5/5, elbow flexion 5/5, elbow extension 5/5, wrist extension 5/5, wrist flexion 5/5, finger abduction 5/5, and hand grip 5/5.
* Lower-limb motor power: Bilateral hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion, great-toe extension, and plantarflexion 5/5.
* Sensory examination: Sensation intact in all four limbs. The preoperative right C6 paraesthesia has improved. No new numbness or saddle sensory disturbance.
* Reflexes: Biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes present and symmetrical. No new pathological reflexes identified.
* Gait and mobility: Not yet fully assessed because the patient is immediately postoperative; able to move all limbs independently in bed. Mobilisation will be assessed once fully recovered from anaesthesia.
* Bladder and bowel function: No preoperative dysfunction. Patient has not yet voided postoperatively; monitor urine output and assess for urinary retention.
* Comparison with preoperative baseline: Motor function is improved to 5/5 in the previously weak right hand. Sensory symptoms are reduced. No new neurological deficit identified.

3. Surgical site and procedure-specific assessment

* Wound: Anterior neck dressing clean, dry, and intact. No active bleeding, expanding swelling, erythema, or discharge.
* Drain: Closed-suction drain patent with approximately 10 mL of serosanguineous output since arrival in recovery. No sudden increase in output.
* Pain: Mild incisional neck pain rated 4/10. No recurrent right arm pain or new radicular symptoms.
* Airway and swallowing: Breathing comfortably on room air. Voice clear. No stridor, respiratory distress, neck tightness, or rapidly increasing swelling. Mild discomfort on swallowing but able to swallow water without coughing or choking.
* Fluid balance: Intravenous fluids ongoing as prescribed. Urine output to be monitored; target is at least 0.5 mL/kg/hour.
* Mobilisation: Bed rest until fully awake, followed by assisted sitting and mobilisation with nursing or physiotherapy support. Avoid sudden neck movements and heavy lifting.

4. Investigations and postoperative review

* Preoperative haemoglobin was 13.8 g/dL, white-cell count 7.4 × 10⁹/L, platelets 248 × 10⁹/L, and creatinine 82 µmol/L.
* Postoperative blood tests are planned for the following morning unless clinically indicated earlier.
* Postoperative cervical spine radiographs are requested to confirm alignment and implant position.
* The operative report confirms satisfactory decompression and stable fixation.
* Continue to review drain output, wound appearance, neurological findings, swallowing, and airway status.

5. Clinical impression

A 50-year-old patient is stable on the day of surgery following uncomplicated C5–C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion with internal fixation. The patient is alert, haemodynamically stable, breathing comfortably, and has no new neurological deficit. Preoperative right-hand weakness and C6 sensory symptoms have improved. The wound is clean and the drain has minimal serosanguineous output. Continued monitoring is required for postoperative neurological deterioration, airway compromise, neck haematoma, dysphagia, infection, and pain.

R — Recommendation

1. Continue vital-sign monitoring and postoperative observations according to the neurosurgical unit protocol.
2. Perform neurological observations hourly initially, including GCS, pupil assessment, bilateral upper- and lower-limb power, sensation, and comparison with the preoperative baseline.
3. Monitor airway, voice, swallowing, neck circumference, and wound swelling closely during the first postoperative hours.
4. Escalate immediately for stridor, respiratory distress, rapidly increasing neck swelling, severe dysphagia, voice deterioration, or suspected expanding haematoma.
5. Continue prescribed multimodal analgesia and reassess pain regularly, aiming for adequate comfort while avoiding excessive sedation.
6. Maintain the wound dressing and inspect it for bleeding, discharge, swelling, erythema, or signs of infection.
7. Measure and document drain output regularly. Notify the neurosurgical team of sudden increased output, fresh blood, or failure of the drain to function.
8. Administer antiemetics as prescribed and prevent vomiting or excessive coughing where possible.
9. Maintain intravenous fluids until oral intake is adequate, then encourage oral fluids as tolerated.
10. Assess swallowing before advancing the diet; begin with clear fluids and progress as tolerated.
11. Mobilise progressively with assistance once fully awake and haemodynamically stable. Encourage safe ambulation and avoid neck hyperextension, heavy lifting, and sudden twisting.
12. Apply mechanical thromboprophylaxis and commence pharmacological thromboprophylaxis only according to the surgeon’s prescription and bleeding-risk assessment.
13. Review postoperative cervical spine radiographs to confirm alignment and satisfactory cage, plate, and screw position.
14. Monitor urine output and confirm spontaneous voiding before discharge from the ward.
15. Escalate urgently for new limb weakness, progressive sensory loss, loss of coordination, severe recurrent radicular pain, new bladder or bowel dysfunction, fever, wound discharge, or altered consciousness.
16. Before discharge, provide instructions regarding wound care, activity restrictions, medication, warning symptoms, follow-up with neurosurgery, and review of postoperative imaging.
